The seven .jpeg files in this folder are tiles of IGN's orthophotos
(BD ORTHO, the layer "Photographies aériennes" of the Géoplateforme),
"IGN – BD ORTHO®"
(https://cartes.gouv.fr/rechercher-une-donnee/dataset/IGNF_BD-ORTHO), under
the Licence Ouverte / Open Licence 2.0. They are not covered by the licence
of the code around them.

Each was recorded on 2026-11-22 between 07:38 and 07:47 UTC with one GET of

    https://data.geopf.fr/wmts?SERVICE=WMTS&REQUEST=GetTile&VERSION=1.0.0&LAYER=ORTHOIMAGERY.ORTHOPHOTOS&STYLE=normal&TILEMATRIXSET=PM_0_19&TILEMATRIX={z}&TILECOL={x}&TILEROW={y}&FORMAT=image/jpeg

with a generic User-Agent, and is kept as it came. The file name is
<where>_<z>_<x>_<y>.jpeg:

    inside_annecy_15_16941_11670        Annecy, wholly inside France
    outside_courmayeur_15_17018_11685   Courmayeur, in Italy: all white,
                                        1651 bytes, byte for byte the tile
                                        over Geneva's centre at zoom 15 and
                                        the one over Turin at zoom 13
    border_veyrier_13_4236_2909         the Swiss border at Veyrier, below
                                        the Salève, at the coarsest zoom
                                        that is passed on: all photograph,
                                        on both sides of the border
    border_veyrier_15_16946_11636       the same, finer
    border_veyrier_19_271142_186184     the same, at the finest zoom: all
                                        photograph, inside France but
                                        within 50 m of the border
    border_montblanc_15_17008_11679     the Italian border on the ridge
                                        west of Mont Blanc's summit: snow
    border_menton_15_17069_11942        the Italian border at the sea at
                                        Menton: the photograph ends in
                                        white some hundred metres beyond it

What the service answered on the same morning, beside these: a tile that
holds nothing of the photographs is a 404 of 137 bytes (XML), not a white
tile (Turin at zoom 14 and 15), and so is a tile at zoom 20, which the
service's set does not have (Annecy). Up to zoom
12 the layer shows the ground beyond France too (Turin at zoom 10, 11 and
12 are pictures of 19 to 21 kB), which is why nothing coarser than zoom 13
is passed on. The photographs reach beyond the border: the tile at
Veyrier at zoom 13, five kilometres wide, is photograph on both sides, and
so is one of a kilometre on the pass of the Petit-Saint-Bernard
(15/17010/11699); the white begins further out.
tests/golden/summary.txt counts what the cut removes of them. On Mont
Blanc the snow on the border itself is white enough to count as the
provider's white, and 1,477 pixels of it are removed within the band.

Each answer carried "cache-control: private, max-age=1814400" and
"access-control-allow-origin: *".

To record them again: fetch the addresses above, then run the tests with
VENTI_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 and look at the PNGs in tests/golden before accepting
them.
